concepts.title: Meaning and Functions of Financial Markets

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning and Functions of Financial Markets' refers to.
questions.a: A financial market is a mechanism that allows people to buy and sell financial securities, commodities and other fungible items of value at low transaction costs and at prices that reflect supply and demand.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning and Functions of Financial Markets'.
questions.a: Financial markets perform the mobilisation of savings, allocation of resources, price discovery and provision of liquidity, thereby linking savers with investors.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Meaning and Functions of Financial Markets' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Financial Markets

concepts.title: Types of Financial Markets -- Money Market and Capital Market

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types of Financial Markets -- Money Market and Capital Market' refers to.
questions.a: The money market deals in short-term funds (up to one year) while the capital market deals in long-term funds (more than one year); together they meet the short-term and long-term financial needs of the economy.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types of Financial Markets -- Money Market and Capital Market'.
questions.a: Money market instruments are liquid and low-risk with short maturities, while capital market instruments are for long-term growth and carry higher risk and return.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Types of Financial Markets -- Money Market and Capital Market' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Types of Financial Markets

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Money Market Instruments' refers to.
questions.a: Money market instruments are short-term, highly liquid, low-risk debt instruments with maturities up to one year, including treasury bills, commercial paper, call money, certificates of deposit and commercial bills.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Money Market Instruments'.
questions.a: Money market instruments help meet short-term financing needs of the government, banks and corporates while providing a parking avenue for short-term surplus funds.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Money Market Instruments' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Money Market Instruments

concepts.title: Capital Market -- Primary and Secondary Market

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Capital Market -- Primary and Secondary Market' refers to.
questions.a: The primary market is where new securities are issued directly to investors (new issue market), while the secondary market is where existing securities are traded among investors (stock market).

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Capital Market -- Primary and Secondary Market'.
questions.a: The primary market raises fresh capital for issuers through public and rights issues, while the secondary market provides liquidity and price discovery to existing securities.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Capital Market -- Primary and Secondary Market' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Capital Market

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Stock Exchange -- Meaning and Functions' refers to.
questions.a: A stock exchange is an institution which provides a platform for the purchase and sale of existing securities such as shares, debentures and bonds, under rules and regulations.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Stock Exchange -- Meaning and Functions'.
questions.a: Stock exchanges provide liquidity and marketability to securities, ensure fair price discovery, promote savings and investment, and support economic growth.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Stock Exchange -- Meaning and Functions' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Stock Exchange

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'SEBI -- Meaning and Objectives' refers to.
questions.a: SEBI is the statutory regulatory body established in 1992 to regulate the securities market in India and protect the interests of investors in securities and promote the development of the securities market.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'SEBI -- Meaning and Objectives'.
questions.a: SEBI's objectives are to protect investors, regulate the securities market and promote its development through fair and transparent practices.

questions.q: Under which section is 'SEBI -- Meaning and Objectives' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Functions of SEBI' refers to.
questions.a: SEBI performs protective, regulatory and developmental functions to safeguard investor interests, ensure orderly market conduct and develop the securities market infrastructure.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Functions of SEBI'.
questions.a: SEBI's protective functions prevent fraud and malpractices, regulatory functions oversee market intermediaries, and developmental functions promote the growth of the securities market.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Functions of SEBI' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Functions of SEBI

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Dematerialisation of Securities' refers to.
questions.a: Dematerialisation (demat) is the process of converting physical share certificates into electronic form held in a demat account with a depository, eliminating the risks associated with physical certificates.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Dematerialisation of Securities'.
questions.a: Dematerialisation removes the risks of loss, theft and damage of physical certificates, enables faster settlement and transfer, and is mandatory for trading in stock exchanges.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Dematerialisation of Securities' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Dematerialisation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Trading in Stock Exchanges' refers to.
questions.a: Trading in stock exchanges is the process of buying and selling securities through registered brokers using the electronic trading system of the exchange, settled through a clearing corporation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Trading in Stock Exchanges'.
questions.a: Trading involves opening a demat and trading account, placing orders through a broker, matching on the exchange's electronic order book, and settlement through the T+1 rolling settlement cycle.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Trading in Stock Exchanges' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Trading in Stock Exchanges

concepts.title: Stock Exchanges in India -- NSE and BSE

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Stock Exchanges in India -- NSE and BSE' refers to.
questions.a: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) are the two principal stock exchanges in India, providing nationwide electronic trading platforms for securities.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Stock Exchanges in India -- NSE and BSE'.
questions.a: NSE introduced screen-based trading and the NIFTY 50 index, while BSE is the oldest stock exchange in Asia with the SENSEX as its benchmark index.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Stock Exchanges in India -- NSE and BSE' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Stock Exchanges in India
